newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark's Codan sees good 96, better 97.
newsitem.headline: Denmark's Codan sees good 96, better 97.

text.p: Danish insurance group Codan said on Friday that it expected 1996 full-year results, due out in March, to show strong profits and predicted still better earnings in 1997.

"Our good investment results in 1996, when shares especially rose sharply, mean that bonus rates for 1997 will rise by one-half percent," Life and Pension director Mogens Andersen wrote in the in-house journal Dialogen.
Codan, 71.45 percent owned by Britain's Royal and Sun Alliance, logged strong 1996 first half results and predicted continued growth in the second six months of the year.
Other executives writing on their departments reported rising pension savings and predicted increased activity in property insurance.
"From the marketing point of view Codan has never been in a better position than that in which it finds itself at the beginning of 1997," sales director Jens Futtrup wrote.
Tough competition dented marine insurance earnings, the journal said, but the marine unit did better than it had expected in retaining clients.
It made no specific forecasts for either 1996 or 1997.
